prompt: A regional airline has lost money for three years. Its planes fly 70% full, while the industry average is 82%. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: Low load factors are likely the main drag on profit.
options.feedback: Right. Flying 70% full against an 82% industry average is a large cost disadvantage. I'd compare load factors and profit by route.

options.text: Planes are probably full, leaving no room for more passengers.
options.feedback: Planes fly 70% full, below the 82% industry average.

options.text: The airline flies too many routes and needs to cut a third of them.
options.feedback: This states a cause as certain and jumps to a drastic cut before any data.

options.text: Fuel costs have likely risen faster than at rivals.
options.feedback: Possible, but nothing points to it. The gap the prompt gives is load factor.

explanation: The data shows planes flying 70% full against an 82% industry average. Likely cause: low load factors drive the losses. To test it, compare load factor and profit by route. If full routes also lose money, look at costs.
